studies.headline: Bison bison has been followed by collar, and the record cannot say whether its timing has changed.
studies.detail: Individual tracks, never published as locations: every published surface is gridded and delayed, and this card carries no coordinate at all.
studies.caveat: Collar effort is not a measured denominator -- a collar goes on an animal someone could catch, in a place they could reach, in a year that was funded. And swapping a radio collar for a GPS collar moves the measured date by 46.8 days, against a trend of order one day per decade.

studies.headline: Pternistis swainsonii occupies about as much of the region as it did thirty years ago.
studies.value: +0.012 in the probability a cell is occupied
studies.detail: Occupancy 0.587 in 1987-1991 against 0.599 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.358 and 0.394.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.

rows.label: Reporting rate, uncorrected
rows.detail: 0.587 to 0.599 — the share of cells the bird was seen in at all, which is what the answer would have been without a detection model

rows.label: Against the other five-year window
rows.detail: 2019-2023 in place of 2008-2012, and the sign agrees

studies.headline: Sterna bergii was recorded almost everywhere in both atlases, so no change can be measured.

studies.headline: Lanius collurio changes direction depending on which five years of the second atlas are used, so this project reports no change for it.
